```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

ggpclient downloads the data of the [GGP data portal](https://www.ggp-i.org), labels it, and stacks the countries of each
round and wave. It is the R version of the Python package
[ggp_client](https://jossl95.github.io/ggp_client/): same steps, same folders, same files.

## The workflow

The access link the portal e-mails you works like a password and is valid for seven days. `p |> ggp_login()` asks for
it (hidden); it is never kept in the environment.

```{r}
library(ggpclient)

p <- ggp_client(project = "ggs", round = 2) # data_dir defaults to "data"

p |> ggp_login()               # paste the access link (hidden); the session is saved
p |> ggp_sync()                # index the portal
ggp_rows(p)                    # one row per file
p |> ggp_download(ext = "dta") # done, skipped, failed
p |> ggp_preprocess()          # each file to parquet + meta.json
p |> ggp_consolidate()         # one parquet per wave, all countries stacked
p |> ggp_stata()               # the same as labelled Stata files
```

## Labels

```{r}
df <- ggp_read("data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet", col_select = c("ggp_country", "dem01"))
meta <- jsonlite::read_json("data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.meta.json")
vl <- meta$value_labels$dem01
df$gender <- factor(df$dem01, levels = as.integer(names(vl)), labels = unlist(vl))
```

Labels are harmonized over the countries, each voting once: a value gets the label more than half of the countries use,
else all labels joined with `" / "`. Codes never change; `original_labels` lists every wording.

## Next to the Python package

Both packages write the same files, so one can read what the other made. The test `tests/testthat/test-equivalence.R`
runs both on the same downloads, the Python one through reticulate, and compares data and labels. Run it with
`RETICULATE_PYTHON` set to a Python that has ggp_client.
